title: Derived semilinear sections and coefficient-linear geometric operations
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] and let $B_1\leftarrow B_2\leftarrow\cdots$ be a strict inverse sequence of sheaves of commutative rings: each $B_n$ is a functor $\mathcal C^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{CommRing}$ whose underlying presheaf of sets is a sheaf, and the transition maps are natural ring homomorphisms. Let $\mathscr S(B)$ have objects $B_n$-module sheaves $M_n$ with $B_{n+1}$-linear maps $M_{n+1}\to\operatorname{Res}_{n+1,n}M_n$, and compatible componentwise maps as morphisms [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars]. Exactness is componentwise. Use unbounded cochain complexes and derived categories [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $\mathbf D(B_n)$ for the enhanced derived module category, meaning the differential graded localization of complexes at quasi-isomorphisms, retaining mapping complexes and their higher composition homotopies, rather than just its ordinary homotopy category $D(B_n)$. A homotopy coherent semilinear section consists of objects of $\mathbf D(B_n)$ and maps to the restricted next objects, with composition homotopies and their higher compatibilities; morphisms retain the same compatibilities. Equivalently these are sections of the derived module-category diagram with forward transition functors $-\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n$, using derived extension/restriction adjunction to write the structure maps in restriction form. For $m\ge n\ge1$, $\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}$ denotes restriction along $B_m\to B_n$. A cartesian section is one for which each adjoint $M_m\otimes^L_{B_m}B_n\to M_n$ is an equivalence [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings].

The enhanced localization of complexes in $\mathscr S(B)$ at componentwise quasi-isomorphisms is equivalent, over all evaluation functors, to this category of homotopy coherent semilinear sections. Its ordinary homotopy category is $D(\mathscr S(B))$. Under the equivalence its cartesian objects are exactly the normalized derived systems. Equivalences are detected by the evaluations. This holds for unbounded complexes and without flatness of $B_m\to B_n$.

Let $u:\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C')\to\operatorname{Sh}(\mathcal C)$ be a morphism of topoi with ring systems $C_n=u^{-1}B_n$ and the specified transition maps. Here a morphism of topoi is an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits. Exact inverse image and its derived right adjoint act on the above section models; their evaluations are the ordinary $u^{-1}$ and $Ru_{*,n}$, with their units and counits. For an open localization the exact extension by zero acts on these models as well [lem-pur-site-restriction-module-adjunction-exact]. Derived coefficient extension and tensor use K-flat representatives and the total tensor complex [def-pc-kflat-complex, def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves]. They and comparisons formed from the above operations, pullback composition identifications, maps of module sheaves, tensor evaluation, and adjunction units and counits have simultaneous enhanced section models. This includes exchange maps obtained as adjunction mates [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], open-extension base-change maps obtained by open adjunction, and composites of these maps with proper direct-image composition. This clause gives models for those specified constructions, without claiming that these comparisons are invertible on arbitrary inputs. In particular the coefficient projection comparison for $Ru_*$, and its composites with open extension, is the derived counit transpose on these models. Evaluation, composition, and taking adjunction transposes preserve these specified constructions and their coherence homotopies. No assertion that evaluation of a K-injective semilinear system is K-injective is part of this statement.

source.place: Tag 079P (theorem-K-injective-embedding-grothendieck), functorial resolution foundation only. The comparison with enhanced varying-ring sections and the simultaneous derived operations are additional agent-formulated localization assertions, not the statement of 079P; they supply the missing coherent construction in the proof of lem-coef-finite-exceptional, paragraphs 2-3.
